reviewed-card-sha256-algorithm: plain sha256 over the card file bytes at commit bdaea43 (`git show bdaea43:tasks/doing/385-...md | shasum -a 256`; the worktree file is byte-identical). This is NOT the CE canonical review digest. The card sits in tasks/doing/ with status doing and declares no blocks:, so ce task validate never reaches the quality-review-receipt check and never computes a canonical digest for it. The canonical digest was confirmed by probe to be a different function of the card — see canonical-digest-probe — and cannot be obtained for this card in its present shape without mutating the card, which would change the very digest being measured.

supersedes.why: that receipt was written mid-review and pinned the card at 99e9ce3, before the implementer folded F1-F3 and the branch was rebased onto master 276988b. Its verdict was conditional and its digest is now stale in both the filename and the reviewed-card-sha256 field.
supersedes.action-requested: delete the superseded file in the same commit that lands this one. The reviewer did not delete it because the lead had already committed it (bdaea43). Leaving two receipts for one card, one of them pinning a digest the card no longer has, is exactly the silent-staleness failure TASK-383's naming convention exists to make loud.

canonical-digest-probe.why: TASK-382's receipt asserted the canonical digest was unobtainable here. This review tested that instead of inheriting it.
canonical-digest-probe.method: copied the card into a scratch board in the session scratchpad, forced status: done plus blocks: [TASK-999] plus a quality-review-receipt pointing at a receipt pinning an all-zero sha, then read the digest the validator names in its mismatch error.
canonical-digest-probe.observed: the validator reported the probe card digests to 52e2956cfd08469dbbc0561b7f025c8d904821aa94b26688b7d4bd5122a40fd1, while that same probe file's plain sha256 was d08670646ac82ea4cb14d8acce2e68868bc45eb47193988b985843862af0346d.
canonical-digest-probe.conclusion: the CE canonical review digest is NOT sha256 over the file bytes. Two further probes — one changing only a frontmatter value, one changing only a body line — each moved the canonical digest, so it covers card content including frontmatter. A canonical digest read out of a mutated copy therefore pins the mutated copy, not this card. The plain digest above is the honest thing to pin, and this field says which digest it is and which commit's bytes it came from.
canonical-digest-probe.correction-to-prior-record: this supersedes the blanket claim that a canonical digest cannot be produced in this repository. It can be produced for any card the validator actually checks (a done card declaring blocks:); what cannot be produced is a canonical digest for a card the validator skips, which is the situation here.
canonical-digest-probe.ce-version: ce 0.8.4 as installed on this workstation
canonical-digest-probe.staleness-warning: this digest pins the card at bdaea43. Closing the card — closing frontmatter plus the zone move to tasks/done/ — will change its bytes and make both this digest and this filename stale. If the card is ever given blocks:, a fresh receipt pinning the canonical digest of the final card is required.
